1:# Continuous bug-hunt workflow
2:
3:Run the bug-hunt cycle continuously: investigate a contract violation, reproduce it, fix the
4:owning boundary, validate, close the change, record, report, and begin the next cycle. Retain and
5:validate tests that invalidate a suspected defect as separate coverage changes.
6:
7:Read applicable [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) files, root [PROJECT.md](PROJECT.md), and this document
8:before acting, including direct invocation of this document. Resolve them from the intended
9:project root, not an assumed VCS root or current invocation directory. Discover actual project
10:contracts and tools; do not assume a language, framework, layout, build system, CI, or VCS.
11:
12:An explicit request to run this workflow authorizes the scoped implementation and validated
13:commits described below, subject to the user's restrictions and `PROJECT.md`. Merely reading,
14:copying, reviewing, or editing this file does not start the loop. This workflow alone does not
15:authorize pushes, installation, deployment, real-user-state tests, or external-service operations.
16:
17:## Constraints and authority
18:
19:- **One defect per cycle.** Select one candidate and fix one owning boundary. Do not bundle
20:  unrelated defects, refactors, or cleanups into the same cycle.
21:- **Evidence over assumption.** Treat notes, commit messages, and earlier records as leads and
22:  baselines, not as proof of current behavior. Re-read source and re-run checks.
23:- **Preserve user work.** Never discard uncommitted edits, untracked files, runtime history, or
24:  test artifacts you do not own. Never use destructive reset/clean operations.
25:- **Smallest coherent change.** Follow repository conventions and preserve public compatibility,
26:  schemas, protocols, persistence, and user-visible behavior unless the defect requires a
27:  deliberate contract change; make such changes explicit and update all affected consumers.
28:- **Do not weaken oracles.** Do not delete, skip, or loosen tests, assertions, lint rules, or
29:  gates to manufacture success. A compile error, skipped test, or invalid expectation is not
30:  evidence.
31:- **Owned state only.** Do not modify real user data, production services, global caches,
32:  credentials, or external accounts. Tests must use owned temporary state.
33:- **No expanded side effects.** Do not push, publish, deploy, install, or change external
34:  infrastructure. This workflow authorizes local implementation, local checks, and scoped commits
35:  only.
36:- **Serialized writers.** Do not run concurrent code-changing hunts or other writers in the same
37:  workspace or history. Do not begin a cycle over unresolved owned edits that would contaminate
38:  its baseline. No locking mechanism is provided; coordinate explicitly.
39:- **Honest reporting.** Never claim a check, commit, or closure happened when it did not. Report
40:  unrun or failing gates as gaps.
41:
42:## Tracking
43:
44:Use exactly one fixed file, `<project root>/HUNT_TRACKING.txt`, recording `Workflow: HUNT_LOOP` in
45:each entry. Read it before selecting or resuming a candidate. Create it if it does not exist. It is
46:append-only: preserve existing records, candidate identifiers, queue entries, inspected areas, and
47:pending work; never rewrite or delete prior history.
48:
49:Each closed, invalidated, or blocked cycle appends a record containing:
50:
51:- date/time and the `Workflow:` name;
52:- candidate identifier, area inspected, and prior leads considered;
53:- suspected defect and the executed evidence (oracle/test and observed result) produced before any
54:  production change;
55:- owning boundary and a summary of the production change and retained tests;
56:- focused and broader validation commands with observed results;
57:- closure: commit/checkpoint identifier, or an explicit statement that none was possible;
58:- status (`CLOSED`, `INVALIDATED`, or `BLOCKED`) and the next queue/pending items.
59:
60:On stop, pause, or interruption, append the exact stage, outstanding changes and checks, and
61:concrete resume instructions instead of leaving the file silent.
62:
63:## 1. Establish the baseline
64:
65:1. Re-read applicable `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`, this workflow, and the tracking file.
66:2. Determine workspace/VCS state: current revision, pre-existing modified and untracked files, and
67:   any runtime history or artifacts you must not disturb. Preserve them.
68:3. Discover the actual build, test, lint/format, and platform gates from project configuration,
69:   `PROJECT.md`, and CI definitions. Do not invent commands.
70:4. Run the baseline gate (or the narrowest applicable subset) before changing production code and
71:   record the result, including pre-existing failures.
72:5. Confirm the baseline is isolated enough to attribute new results to this cycle. If unresolved
73:   owned edits would contaminate it, stop and record the blocker rather than guessing.
74:
75:## 2. Select a candidate
76:
77:Choose one specific, testable suspected contract violation:
78:
79:- resume a pending candidate from `HUNT_TRACKING.txt`, or inspect an area not yet settled there;
80:- state the violated contract, the owning boundary, and the observable oracle that would
81:  distinguish correct from incorrect behavior;
82:- prefer a candidate whose baseline and fix remain within one component and can be validated with
83:  deterministic, offline tests;
84:- do not repeat a settled lead without new evidence, and do not invent a defect to keep busy.
85:
86:If inspection finds no testable candidate, record the inspected areas and broaden the search within
87:the authorized scope rather than inventing a defect.
88:
89:## 3. Reproduce and confirm
90:
91:Before changing production code, add the most focused deterministic test that demonstrates the
92:suspected defect, and run it. Record the actual failing output in the tracking file.
93:
94:- Use owned temporary fixtures and avoid network access or real external state.
95:- A failure caused by a compile error, a skipped/disabled test, an invalid expectation, or an
96:  unrelated pre-existing defect does not confirm the candidate; correct the test or discard the
97:  candidate.
98:- If the evidence invalidates the suspicion, do not change production code. If the test asserts
99:  intended existing behavior, keep it as a retained coverage change, record the invalidation
100:  evidence, and close the cycle as `INVALIDATED`.
101:- Never weaken the oracle to obtain a fix.
102:
103:## 4. Fix the owning boundary
104:
105:Implement the smallest coherent production change at the boundary that owns the contract:
106:
107:- follow repository conventions for naming, architecture, error handling, resource cleanup, and
108:  state transitions;
109:- preserve compatibility and data integrity, and update every affected consumer if a contract
110:  genuinely changes;
111:- update generated sources through their generator rather than editing generated output;
112:- avoid unrelated refactoring, speculative abstractions, dead scaffolding, debug code, and new
113:  TODOs;
114:- update authoritative documentation and fixtures when behavior or contracts change.
115:
116:## 5. Validate
117:
118:Run, at minimum:
119:
120:1. the focused regression test(s) from step 3, now passing;
121:2. the project's full test gate discovered in step 1;
122:3. formatter/linter/static-analysis and packaging gates required by `PROJECT.md` or CI;
123:4. any component-specific check the project requires (for example, a terminal-emulation check for
124:   TUI changes);
125:5. `git diff --check` and a full review of the diff when Git is present; otherwise an explicit
126:   inventory of every modified path.
127:
128:Do not claim success while a required gate fails or remains unrun. Distinguish new failures from
129:the recorded baseline and report remaining risks.
130:
131:## 6. Close the change
132:
133:When the implementation is validated:
134:
135:- stage only the files owned by this cycle; do not stage unrelated user edits;
136:- commit with a descriptive message following project conventions (including any required
137:  sign-off), if the workflow invocation authorized commits and a usable VCS exists;
138:- leave `HUNT_TRACKING.txt` as the untracked running record unless the project explicitly tracks
139:  it;
140:- if no VCS exists, do not initialize one; report the change inventory and the missing commit
141:  capability;
142:- never push, publish, deploy, or install.
143:
144:If validation cannot be completed, leave the work uncommitted, preserve the useful tests, and
145:record the cycle as `BLOCKED`.
146:
147:## 7. Record and report
148:
149:Append the record described in [Tracking](#tracking), then report to the user:
150:
151:- the candidate and the observed evidence;
152:- the owning boundary and files changed;
153:- the exact checks run and their observed results, distinguishing new failures from baseline;
154:- the commit or checkpoint, or why none was possible;
155:- remaining gaps, risks, and anything the user must authorize.
156:
157:## 8. Continuous cadence
158:
159:This section defines when the next cycle starts; it does not override the constraints, procedure,
160:validation, closure, or tracking rules above.
161:
162:After each validated fix or retained-coverage change is closed, append its evidence to
163:`HUNT_TRACKING.txt`, send an intermediate progress report, then return immediately to
164:[baseline discovery](#1-establish-the-baseline). Do not ask for per-cycle confirmation or stop
165:merely because one cycle succeeded. Each candidate gets a fresh baseline, oracle, checks, and
166:separate closure; do not combine defects or amend prior cycles.
167:
168:If a candidate is blocked, record the reason and preserve useful tests/work. Investigate another
169:independent candidate only if its baseline can be isolated safely. Report and stop when unresolved
170:constraints, environment, authorization, ownership, validation, or closure prevent all further
171:safe progress. A problem affecting one candidate does not automatically block unrelated safe work.
172:
173:If inspection finds no testable candidate, record the inspected areas and broaden the search within
174:the authorized scope. Do not invent a defect or weaken the oracle to obtain a fix. Keep the queue
175:and settled leads in the tracker so repeated cycles produce new evidence rather than repeating the
176:same inspection.
177:
178:Continue until the user stops/pauses the workflow or a blocker prevents all further safe progress.
179:Respect explicit run limits and higher-priority tool/environment limits; persistence never expands
180:authorization or justifies skipped checks. Send progress updates during investigation and
181:validation.
182:
183:On stop, pause, or interruption, stop starting work, clean up owned resources when possible, and
184:append the exact stage, outstanding changes/checks, and resume instructions to
185:`HUNT_TRACKING.txt`. Leave incomplete work uncommitted, preserve valid coverage, and summarize
186:actual completed commits/checkpoints and remaining work. A future invocation reads this same
187:history and reinspects the project before resuming.
